title: Guarded reservation contours and autoscale contracts PRD
creator: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary:
This PRD introduces 'Reservation Contours' and 'Autoscale Contracts' for Redwood Dedicated capacity. The goal is to provide customers deterministic reserved throughput while allowing safe, measurable burst behavior and graceful cross-tenant isolation when capacity is constrained.

Problem statement:
Customers with reserved Dedicated capacity need predictable latency and throughput guarantees for production traffic, but also want: (1) occasional short bursts beyond reservation without manual ops, (2) budgeted safety for noisy neighbors, and (3) clear semantics when preemption occurs. Current behavior is all-or-nothing: hard reservations with brittle fallback or overly permissive bursts that risk SLOs for others.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Provide a contract model customers can purchase that defines reserved baseline, guaranteed headroom, and burst rules in clear SLA terms.
- Allow safe, automated short-term autoscale above reservation with tenant-level banked credits and backpressure policies that preserve cluster SLOs.
- Expose controls in Console and API for configuring contour shapes (steady baseline, soft headroom, emergency credit) and viewable metrics to trace reservations -> real consumption.
- Roll out with telemetry and behavioral alerts to detect regressions in 99th percentile latency for co-located tenants.

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Full redesign of underlying scheduler kernel. This PRD relies on current capacity allocator primitives and targeted runtime changes in ENG-52411.
- Cross-region capacity pooling.

Proposal overview:
1) Reservation Contours: a compact config object that describes how a tenant's capacity behaves over time. Contour fields (API/Console):
   - baseline_units: reserved steady units (tokens/sec or tokens/s-equivalent)
   - guaranteed_headroom: short-lived guaranteed uplift (units, time window)
   - burst_health_threshold: metric threshold (error rate/latency) that gates burst continuation
   - banked_credits: numeric credit balance that can be consumed for bursts beyond headroom
   - preemption_priority: ordinal that participates in eviction when cluster pressure happens

2) Autoscale Contracts: a purchasable SLA mapping contour to billing and enforcement semantics. Contract elements:
   - allowed_burst_ratio: ratio above baseline that is billable at burst rate
   - commit_window: contract duration (monthly/quarterly)
   - grace_runway: cumulative seconds of burst allowed before enforced throttle or preemption

3) Banked Credits & 'Entropy-safe' Fallbacks:
   - Tenants earn credits over time when under baseline. Credits can be consumed to smooth spikes. Credits decay to avoid permanent hoarding.
   - When cluster-wide pressure is detected, a staged fallback runs: soft-degrade (reduce guaranteed_headroom), credit-only mode (prevent new headroom grants), and finally preemption according to preemption_priority.

4) Console + API UX:
   - New 'Reservation' page per tenant showing Contour graph (baseline/headroom/credits), recent consumption, and forecasted burn rate.
   - REST API: PUT /dedicated/reservations/{tenant} accepting contour JSON and returning contract id.
   - Billing mapping: new usage rows showing baseline vs burst units consumed.

Engineering changes required (high level):
- Runtime: implement credit bank accounting, headroom enforcement, and preemption hook (ENG-52411).
- Orchestration: integrate contour enforcement into scheduler and autoscale loop (ENG-52900).
- Console: new UI surfaces and graphs (DES-20341 for design artifacts).
- Billing: support two-tier metering lines (baseline vs burst).

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
1) API: Create/Update/Delete reservation contour via API with validation and immediate enforcement in sandbox.
2) Baseline guarantee: Under synthetic test traffic, tenant receiving baseline_units must sustain target p50/p95 latency within agreed SLA 99% of test window (e.g., p95 <= 250ms for 10k tokens/min baseline).
3) Guaranteed headroom: When a tenant generates traffic within guaranteed_headroom window, the system must route and serve without preemption for the duration of the window at least 98% of the time in cluster with <=70% utilization.
4) Banked credits: Credits accrue at configured rate during baseline idle periods and can be consumed; behavior validated by credit balance metrics and a test harness that consumes credits to maintain throughput beyond headroom.
5) Fallback ordering: Under induced cluster pressure tests, confirmed ordering of (a) soft-degrade headroom, (b) credit-only mode, (c) preemption by priority — observed and logged in audit events.
6) Billing: Burst consumption appears on usage reports and aligns with recorded burst_units in the metering pipeline within 1% in synthetic tests.
7) Console: Reservation page shows contour timeline and forecasted burn with no UX blocking issues in usability testing (N=6 PM/SE/Customer).

Scope changes / trade-offs discussed so far:
- Initial scope excluded per-request token-weighted accounting; we added a light-weight token-estimate multiplier to provide more accurate burst billing. This increased engineering effort by ~2 points.
- We deliberately avoid complicated predictive autoscaling in v1 (no ML-based forecast). The decision reduces rollout risk but may under-utilize headroom in some customers.

Rollout plan & guardrails:
- Phase 0 (alpha): Internal tenants + 3 pilot customers; manual monitoring and manual fallback overrides.
- Phase 1 (beta): Wider opt-in with Console controls and billing preview; telemetry collection for 30 days.
- Phase 2 (GA): Enabled by default for customers with Dedicated contracts; automatic enforcement and billing.
- Safety gates: GA only if cluster-level 99th latency regressions are <= 2% relative to baseline and no more than 1 high-severity isolation regression in pilot cohort.

Observability & Metrics to ship:
- Reservation consumption per-tenant time series (baseline, headroom, burst_units, credits_balance).
- Latency P50/P95/P99 for each tenant and co-located tenants when bursts occur.
- Preemption events and time-to-fall-through from soft-degrade to preemption.
- Billing delta: reported vs computed burst units.

Security & Compliance notes:
- All audit events for reservation changes, preemption, and credit consumption must be logged to customer audit logs (KMS encrypted).
- Security review required for the API changes that expose tenant metrics to ensure no cross-tenant leakage (see ENG-54102 security spike).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the default credit accrual rate per baseline unit? Recommend conservative 10% per 24h for v1; needs financial modeling.
- Are credits transferable between sub-tenants under the same org? (Conservative approach: no, initially).
- How should emergency manual overrides be surfaced to SRE/Oncall? (Runbook draft attached).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Priya Kapoor (owner), Maya Chen (PM lead)
- Engineering: Ravi Singh (runtime), Elena Markov (scheduler), Kevin Park (billing)
